page: Microsoft Azure F64alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the configuration provisions 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem is supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core, alongside vector extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support. Memory capacity is allocated at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, providing 128.0 GB of system memory, or 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 7560 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and operates without an attached GPU or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across dense computational workloads. The platform scored 2865.0 in Geekbench single-core and 31093.0 in multi-core testing, complemented by a PassMark CPU score of 115141.66 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 231048.41. Memory throughput remains substantial despite the compute focus, logging 415.58 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB block reads and 205.55 GB/sec in writes. Software compilation via Clang achieved a score of 85650.0, and static web serving throughput reached 96.82 GB/sec. Low-parameter machine learning workloads show high prompt processing efficiency, measuring 5746.06 tokens per second on a 135M model and 298.62 tokens per second on a 7B model using CPU vector extensions.

The F64alds_v7 provides strong compute and local I/O density by coupling non-hyperthreaded physical cores with 7560 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. The primary tradeoff lies in the memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU, which limits utility for large in-memory footprints. The architecture is best suited for compute-heavy parallel workloads, batch processing, Clang software builds, video rendering, scientific simulations, and high-throughput web serving requiring substantial fast scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure F64alds_v7 is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 64-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with dedicated physical cores and no multithreading, it features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, BF16, and VNNI. The system is provisioned with 128.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a bundled 7560 GB local NVMe SSD, but contains no GPU. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier raw compute and compiler metrics, recording 31093.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 85650.0 in Clang build tests, along with 415.58 GB/sec memory read bandwidth. Although restricted for memory-heavy datasets due to its 1:2 CPU-to-RAM balance, the hardware profile delivers exceptional per-core compute efficiency and fast local I/O, making it well-suited for high-concurrency batch processing, software compilation, analytics pipelines, and high-traffic web serving.
